items.title: Ramsey Lewis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The interviewee Ramsey Lewis does not mention Franklin Delano Roosevelt in his speech. FDR is only mentioned by the interviewer in a narrative context regarding Obama and A. Philip Randolph.

ctx.x: what’s going on, because they either don’t want to know or they don’t take time to know what’s good about our country and what needs improving in our country. You asked me about music coming back, and jazz, and the African-American experience. It’ll come back, but there are things to be dealt with, I think.

We have seen some – what, as an optimist, that gives me hope, a glimmer of hope, and that is we’ve seen members of the working class in Wisconsin stand up. We’ve seen now that they’re having demonstrations down on Wall Street. I remember when Obama – shortly after he was elected, he quoted FDR – Franklin Delano Roosevelt – saying – who had met with A. Philip Randolph. A. Philip Randolph was trying to get him to get on board with desegregation. He said, “Make me do it. You make me do it.” That’s what Obama said to…

I think the system is bigger than we think it is. I think we don’t really know where the system is. I think – I read a book some time ago that there are 400 families around the world – I think it was fiction, but it was based on fact – 400 families or 400 groups
